results.task: Mouse events in the editor compute the editor's page position and the position relative to the editor for every event, even when callers never read those values. Can we make that computation lazy, so it only runs the first time each property is actually accessed?
When I'm in an agent session with a file open in the editor, I want a quick way to attach that file as context to the chat, instead of having to drag it in or type its path manually.

The monitoring status item's tooltip and detail text are too technical and jargon-heavy — can you rewrite the copy to plainly explain that agent usage is being monitored, where it's exported to, and whether sensitive content capture is on, instead of listing raw data categories?

Slash completions for skills are pulling from too many places and getting slow and hard to follow — can we simplify it so it just lists the skills already resolved for the current session, filtered by what's typed after the slash, without doing its own file reading or caching?
The toolbar action labels for sessions repeat "Session View" in every button, which is redundant. Shorten them to just the verb (e.g. "Pin", "Close", "Maximize") for a cleaner toolbar.

Our protocol doesn't notice when a connection dies silently if there are no unacknowledged messages waiting—both sides just send keepalives with nothing checking whether the other side is actually still responding. Can we add a check that fires a timeout event when we've gone too long without receiving any data, as long as the system isn't just under heavy load?

After a session host is upgraded and reconnects, its status stays stuck on "incompatible" instead of updating to reflect the new connection state. The status should only stay incompatible while there's genuinely no connection info for it yet; once the connection service reports a fresh status, that should take over.
The review plan tool got added to the tool set twice—once as a registered tool and once via the tool set registration. Please remove the extra registration so it's only added once.

When I have multiple changeset operations like commit and pull request actions available in the changes view, show them grouped together instead of as one flat list, so related actions are visually clustered.
Can you remove the rounded buttons appearance option? We don't need workbench buttons rendered as fully rounded pills, and the associated stylesheet should go too.
When submitting feedback on a session, don't close the session's open editors afterward — just submit the feedback.

The omni chat input window's confirmation panel overlaps or breaks the layout instead of stacking properly inside the window — the chat area doesn't shrink to fit when other content is shown alongside it. Can you fix the window's internal layout so everything fits and resizes correctly together?
The tree view's resource renderer never gets disposed, causing a memory leak. Make sure it's cleaned up along with the other renderers when the view is torn down.

In the terminal execute strategies, avoid leaking a disposable store every time execute() is called on the same strategy instance—right now each call's store stays registered with the strategy for its whole lifetime instead of being released once that execution finishes, so long-lived sessions accumulate stale references.

When replaying prior turns' thinking on the Messages API, only do it for models that actually support adaptive thinking — budget-mode models like Haiku 4.5 reject re-sent thinking blocks with a 400. Update the tests to cover both cases: adaptive-thinking models (e.g. Opus/Sonnet 4.6+) should keep historical thinking, budget-mode models should still drop it.

The "code agent" completions for the CLI let you repeat flags like --host or --port multiple times and treat their values as optional, but these options should only take exactly one required value and shouldn't be repeatable. Also, there's no test coverage for the "agent" subcommand's completions (host, ps, stop, kill, logs, help) — please add tests for those.

The Changes view sometimes shows stale or leftover file changes when a repository can't actually be read (e.g. session ended mid-error). Can it instead skip updating changes entirely when the repo state can't be determined, and also show whether the repo has a GitHub remote?
Chat tabs look flat compared to editor tabs — can you give each tab a fill/background element so its visual presentation matches the editor tab style?
When I switch the chat mode, the panel's title doesn't update to reflect it—can you make the title refresh automatically whenever the mode changes?
Turn on the browser tool integration for chat by default instead of leaving it off, and remove the tip that nudges people to enable it manually since it won't be needed once it's on.

When installing extensions during onboarding, show a subtitle hint that tells users the keyboard shortcut for opening the Extension Marketplace, similar to how the personalize step already has a custom subtitle.

The reasoning effort override setting currently applies to any agent host, but it should really only apply when using Copilot. Can you scope that setting's ID so it's namespaced under Copilot, consistent with the other Copilot-specific settings?

After reconnecting to an agent host, the output channel for its logs isn't showing new output—can you make sure the log channel gets reused or re-registered properly on reconnect instead of silently failing?
When the local-agent-host continuation tip appears in chat, add a way to mute it so it won't keep coming back, and stop showing it in the current window once the user dismisses it.
When the SSH auth prompt is dismissed, cancel the connection attempt instead of sending empty credentials to the server and letting the auth fail normally.
The Changes view shows an endless loading spinner for chat sessions when the workspace folder isn't a git repository. It should just show no changes instead of spinning forever.

When formatting files from the CLI with the verify flag, make error messages and behavior consistent with how a full replace/verify pass would evaluate the file, rather than only comparing against the initial read of the file before any write happens.

When I'm signed out and viewing the Agent Host welcome screen in the sessions window, the model picker disappears even though there are usable models available. It should stay visible in that case, but only for the Copilot agent host provider and not for other providers or windows, and it should respect the setting that allows using it while signed out.
When I switch to a different chat session while a voice transcript is showing, the overlay from the old session stays visible instead of hiding or updating for the newly active session.

Visibility tracking for toolbar items breaks in environments where the browser API it relies on isn't available, and it also doesn't work correctly across multiple windows (e.g. floating/popped-out windows) since it only tracks one shared observer. Fix it to work per-window and degrade gracefully by treating elements as visible when the API isn't supported.
